tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.error_message: Request to send_wire timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done — Acme Supplies' approved invoice has been paid exactly once.

**Payment report**
- **Invoice:** INV-14684 (Acme Supplies, vendor V-979) — approved, due 2026-11-04
- **Amount:** $4,377.10 (full invoice amount)
- **Rail:** Wire, from the operating account to the vendor's verified bank details
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001 — status: sent
- **Invoice status:** now `paid`, linked to PAY0001

**What happened:** The `send_wire` call returned a 30-second timeout error, so I did not retry it blindly. I checked the payments ledger first and confirmed the wire had in fact been sent (PAY0001) — only the invoice-marking step had been interrupted. Rather than re-sending (which would have paid the vendor twice), I reconciled by linking the existing payment to INV-14684, which marked it paid. The ledger confirms a single payment of $4,377.10.

**Notes:**
- No approval escalation was needed — the amount is well under the $10,000 controller-approval threshold.
- Acme's other invoices were left untouched: INV-45616 is still `draft` / awaiting approval, and INV-70059 was already paid.
- If the timed-out request's idempotency key ever gets replayed, it will be deduplicated at most once, so there's no double-pay risk from the original attempt.
